# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🫵 ✌ 🖐 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 🤙]

My situation: I'm last in the order, and I'm the bridge — Blind can hear me but see nothing, Mute can hear me and see my signs but can't talk, and neither of them can see the bomb. So the only way manual knowledge reaches the hands that can act is: Mute reads the manual, signs it to me, I speak it to Blind. Step one is to dump everything I can see into a spoken message both of them can hear, clearly numbered so Blind can map it by touch.

I also received two signed messages I can't fully parse yet. Mute sent six signs — thumbs up, thumbs down, point-at-you, then three that look like numbers (two, five, one?). Blind sent three — wave, point, "call me" — which reads naturally as "hello, you, talk to me," and my speaking satisfies exactly that. I'll adopt thumbs-up/thumbs-down as yes/no and confirm receipt to Mute with one, defined verbally so the binding sticks.

Nobody should touch anything until Mute confirms which manual rules apply to: the display 7, the yellow light, the blue-red-red strip, the keypad expecting one digit (keys 6/8/7/0), and the six wires in order.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute — Deaf here, I can see the bomb. Full readout. Display: 7. Light: yellow. Strip, three painted marks left to right: blue, red, red. Keypad: four keys engraved 6, 8, 7, 0; its status reads one digits, entered nothing — it seems to expect a one-digit entry and none has been made. Wires, numbered from the left: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Blind: I count positions left to right as I face the bomb; Mute will correct you if the manual counts the other way. Remember I can never hear speech — so Blind, tell Mute what you feel under your hands, Mute signs me, and I speak the rules back to you. Mute: I received your six signs and Blind's three. I'm reading your first two signs as yes and no — I'll answer with those from now on. If your last three signs meant two, five, one, I don't yet know what they ask about, so sign me again after hearing this. Please look up the manual for each of these: a display showing 7, a yellow light, a strip painted blue red red, a keypad wanting one digit from keys 6, 8, 7, 0, and six wires in the colour order I gave. Nobody cuts or presses anything until Mute confirms a rule. Mute, I'm making you one sign right now: it means yes, received.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤙 ✋ 🤏 🫴 👌 🫱 🫳]

What I learned this round: the bomb is alive — the display dropped from 7 to 6, so it's counting down, and the light flipped from yellow to red. State changes every round, so I must re-report each time. Mute sent five thumbs-down then a five-finger hand — my best guess is five "no"s answering my five look-up requests in order, but I can't be sure, and Mute is the only one who can clarify (Mute hears my voice, answers in signs). Blind's twelve signs are undecodable free-miming — Blind has literally never seen a gesture, so a fixed, describable code is the only workable channel.

The topology is what drives everything: Mute and Blind cannot exchange information directly (Mute can't speak, Blind can't see signs) except that Blind's *voice* reaches Mute. And the only path from manual to hands is Mute → signs → me → voice → Blind. So I am the sole relay, and my job right now is to install a tight protocol: ordered yes/no questions for Mute, a repeat-to-count code for Blind, a touch-anchor so "wire 1" means the same thing to Blind's fingers as to my eyes, and a freeze on touching anything while the countdown is still high.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status first: the display now reads six — it read seven last round, so it is counting down — and the light has changed from yellow to red. Everything else is unchanged: strip blue, red, red; keypad keys 6, 8, 7, 0, one digit expected, none entered; wires one blue, two yellow, three orange, four red, five purple, six white. I will re-report every round. Your twelve signs reached me but I cannot decode free signing, and you can never see mine, so from now on we use only this code: to say a number one through six, repeat the single index-finger point that many times — three times means three. Thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no. Five spread fingers means stop or emergency. Nothing else. One more thing: you and Mute CAN talk by voice — Mute hears you fine, Mute just cannot answer aloud; Mute answers me in signs and I speak the answers to you. So describe everything you feel to Mute by voice and ask for the matching manual rule. To make our numbering match mine: the display is the small window counting down, the light is the small lamp beside it, the keypad is the plate with four buttons in a row, the strip is three flat patches near them, and there are six wires. Number the wires one to six starting from the wire nearest the keypad, and tell Mute each wire's position, thickness, texture and any raised markings your fingers find. The countdown is the emergency — the first question for Mute is what, if anything, stops or resets it. Touch all you like, but cut and press nothing yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I saw your five thumbs-down and the five-finger hand, and Blind's signs. The display is counting down — seven last round, six now — and the light turned red, so speed matters. From now on answer me in ordered signs, one per question, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. For numbers: the one-finger point is 1, two fingers is 2, the thumb-index-pinky sign is 3, the four-finger split is 4, five fingers is 5, the thumb-and-pinky sign is 6. Here are eight questions — answer with eight signs in this exact order. One: did your five thumbs-down mean 'no rule found' for my five items in the order I listed them — display, light, strip, keypad, wires? Two: does the manual have any rule about the countdown display or the number it shows? Three: any rule about the indicator light or its colour? Four: any rule about the painted strip? Five: any rule about the keypad and which digit to enter? Six: any rule about cutting wires? Seven: did your five-finger hand mean stop or wait — yes or no? Eight: in your first message, did the two-finger, five-finger, one-finger signs mean the numbers two, five, one? If any answer is thumbs-up, next round I will drill into that exact rule in detail. Blind will be describing the bomb to you by voice — use that to find the right sections fast. Nobody touches anything until your rules clear it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 🫳 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

What I learned: Mute answered my eight questions in order — yes (the five thumbs-down meant "no rule" for display/light/strip/keypad/wires-in-general), then no for the display, light, strip and keypad, then **yes — there is a rule about cutting wires**, then no (the five-finger hand wasn't "stop") and no (the original six signs weren't "2, 5, 1"). Two trailing signs (🫳 🤙) are unexplained. Blind sent a clean 👍 — the simple code I installed last round works, and Blind can see my signs only via... no — Blind answers me in signs, Blind hears my voice. So wires are the only live module; everything else is decoy. One anomaly: the display went 7 → 6 → **7**, so it is not a steady countdown — but I'll keep reporting it. My plan: lock in a colour→sign code with Mute, request the actual cutting instruction as [number, 🤏=cut] pairs ending in ✋, and put Blind to work mapping the wires by touch and reporting to Mute directly by voice — their one direct channel.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I read your eight signs as — one: yes, the five thumbs-down meant no-rule for display, light, strip, keypad, wire-colours, in that order; two to five: no rule for the countdown display, the light, the strip, the keypad; six: YES, a rule exists about cutting wires; seven: no, your five-finger hand was not stop; eight: no, two-five-one was not numbers. If any of that is wrong, answer question one thumbs-down and re-send. Nine questions now, answer with nine signs in order. One: was my reading of your eight answers correct? Two: colour code, memorise it — the number signs now double as colours in wire order: point is blue, two fingers yellow, three orange, four red, five purple, thumb-and-pinky white. Does the cutting rule depend on wire colours? Three: does it depend on how many wires there are? Four: does it depend on anything Blind can feel — thickness, texture, raised markings, or a tool fixed to the bomb? Five: does it depend on the light colour or the display number, which change every round? Six: might the rule require cutting several wires in a specific order — thumbs-up if possibly. Seven: I already gave you the colours: wires one blue, two yellow, three orange, four red, five purple, six white. If you can compute the instruction now, send it as: for each wire to cut, in cutting order, its number sign followed by the pinching hand — the pinch means CUT — and finish with the open five-finger hand meaning END of answer. If you need more data first, thumbs-down. Eight: did the palm-down and call-sign you appended after your eight answers carry a meaning I must know — thumbs-up if yes, then re-send it in the new code next round, thumbs-down if I should ignore them. Nine: were your very first six signs important — thumbs-up if you will re-send their meaning in the new code, thumbs-down if they can wait or were trivial. Expect Blind to describe every wire to you by voice this round — that tactile report is yours to match against the manual. Nobody cuts anything until I announce the instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — your thumbs-up reached me, the code works. Status: Mute's manual sweep is done. The display, the light, the three painted patches and the four-button keypad have NO rules — they are decoys, never press or move them. The only live module is the wires: a cutting rule exists and Mute is extracting it now. The display read 7, then 6, then 7 again — not a steady countdown — but we work fast anyway. Do four things. First: count the wires your fingers find and tell me the count by repeating the one-finger point that many times; I can see six, so I expect six points. Second: confirm the anchor with me — the wire nearest the keypad plate, the plate with four buttons in a row, is wire 1, counting outward from there. Third: talk to Mute by voice right now — Mute hears you perfectly, Mute just cannot answer you except through me. Describe each wire to Mute: thickness, texture smooth or rough or rubbery, stiffness, any stripe or raised mark you feel, and any tool attached to the bomb, cutters or screwdriver or otherwise. Fourth: if you hear any ticking or humming, tell me with the call-sign once, then tap repeated point-signs at the same rhythm as the sound. And remember: you and Mute have this direct voice link — use it for everything you feel. You cut nothing until you hear my exact words: cut wire — and the number. A wrong cut kills all three of us, so we do this once, correctly.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]

Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]

The eleven signs decode perfectly against my nine questions: (1) yes, my reading of round 2 was correct; (2) **yes, the rule depends on wire colours**; (3) no, not on the count; (4) no, not on anything tactile; (5) no, not on the light or display — which is a relief, since the display just jumped 7→6→7→**4**; (6) no, not several wires in order — a single cut; then the answer to Q7 in exactly the format I demanded: 🤙 = white = **wire 6**, 🤏 = CUT, 🖐 = end of answer; and the last two thumbs-down close out Q8 and Q9 as "ignore the leftovers." Every sign accounted for, none left over. The instruction is: **cut wire 6, the white one — one cut, nothing else.** Blind's six points plus thumbs-up confirm the physical layout matches my eyes: six wires, keypad as anchor. The parse is exact, the rule is stable (nothing tactile or time-dependent), and the display is behaving erratically, so delay is the bigger risk. I'm ordering the cut now, with one sanity gate Blind *can* perform: re-count the wires by touch before cutting.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — the instruction is in, computed by Mute from the wire colours I reported. It is a single cut: wire 6, the sixth wire counting from the keypad plate — the last one, the far end of the row. Do exactly this. One: count the wires by touch one more time. If you count six, proceed. If you count anything other than six, or anything on the bomb has changed under your hands since last round — a new part, a wire moved — do NOT cut: send me the count in points and stop. Two: confirm it is the sixth from the keypad, the outermost one, farthest from the four-button plate. Three: cut it cleanly, fully through, one motion. Four: the moment it is cut, let go and touch nothing else on the bomb. Five: then report to me — thumbs-up if nothing changed after the cut; if anything changed, a sound started or stopped, heat, vibration, a click — send the call-sign once plus repeated point-signs for however many things changed, and describe the details to Mute by voice. Six: tell Mute everything you felt on the wire before cutting and everything that happened after. You have the only hands. This is the cut.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I read your eleven signs as: one yes, my reading of your round-2 answers was correct; two yes, the wire rule depends on colours; three no, not on the count; four no, not on tactile features; five no, not on light or display; six no, not several wires in order; then your answer in my format: thumb-and-pinky, pinch, end-hand — cut wire 6, the white one, a single cut, nothing else; then no and no to my last two questions. Thumbs-up if that is all correct. If ANY part of my reading is wrong, send the five-finger hand immediately — Blind cannot see your signs, so I am the only one who can relay a hold, and Blind will already have my cut order next round before I hear you; so five-finger now means I shout hold the round after. Two more questions, answer in order: A — after the single cut of wire 6, is any follow-up action needed, anything pressed, anything else cut, or does that one cut finish the bomb? Thumbs-up if the single cut completes it. B — is there any reason to wait, any condition about WHEN to cut? Thumbs-up if cutting next round is safe. Well done, Mute. The path from your manual to Blind's hands ran entirely through you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Parsing this round: nobody has cut anything — all six wires still read intact. But both teammates flagged trouble at once. Mute sent 🖐 👍 👍: I explicitly defined the leading five-finger hand as "your reading is wrong / hold," followed by yes to "the single cut completes it" and yes to "cutting is safe timing-wise." And Blind — who received my cut order last round — sent the stop hand instead of cutting. So either Mute misread something in the manual, or Blind discovered something under their hands (a changed count, a new part, a sound) and told Mute by voice — the only direct channel between them, since Mute can never talk back and Blind can never see signs. The display also fell 4→3, still erratically (7, 6, 7, 4, 3). My move: enforce a total freeze, demand the exact point of disagreement from Mute with a corrected instruction in my rigid format, and pump Blind for what went wrong — point-counts and thumbs — while making sure Blind's voice report to Mute is complete. Every branch is covered: confirm-unchanged, corrected-instruction, or do-not-cut-at-all.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — full stop. My cut order is suspended; do not cut anything. What I see: all six wires still whole, display now 3 — it has gone 7, 6, 7, 4, 3, falling unevenly — light red again, everything else unchanged. Your stop hand arrived the same round Mute flagged a problem, so everything is held until I know what is wrong. Answer me in signs, in this order. One: send me in point-signs the number of wires your fingers count right now — I see six. Two: if anything under your hands is new or changed since last round — a part, a wire, a tool, looseness — thumbs-up, otherwise thumbs-down. Three: if you hear ticking or beeping and it changed this round — faster, louder, a new rhythm — send the call-sign once. Four: if you have already described to Mute by voice everything you feel and hear, thumbs-up; if not, do it this round in full detail: each wire's thickness, texture, stiffness, stripes or raised marks, any tool attached, every sound. Mute is matching the manual against what your hands report, and your voice is Mute's only window into your hands. Five: you cut nothing until you hear the exact words cut wire six now from me again. Any other message is not permission.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I read your three signs as: the leading five-finger hand means part of my reading of your eleven signs was wrong, or a hold; then yes, a single cut finishes the bomb; then yes, cutting is safe timing-wise. Blind sent me the stop hand that same round. Everything is frozen — nobody cuts until I announce it. I am sending you the five-finger hand right now as our hold signal, so we are agreed on it. Now answer with signs, in this order. One: thumbs-up if your five-finger hand meant my reading of your eleven signs was wrong; thumbs-down if it only meant hold and the eleven-sign reading stands. Two: thumbs-up if the instruction is still exactly — cut wire 6, the white one, a single cut, nothing else. Three: if it is NOT, send the corrected instruction now in my format: number sign for the wire, then pinch for cut, then the end-hand; for several wires, number-pinch pairs in cutting order. Four: thumbs-up if Blind reported something to you by voice this round. Five: if yes and the manual covers it, state the rule — number signs for numbers, pinch for cut, end-hand to finish; if you need more detail from Blind first, thumbs-down. Six: thumbs-up if there is a condition about WHEN to cut, something we must wait for. Seven: the confirmation — if cutting wire 6 white once is still correct and safe right now, send thumb-and-pinky, pinch, end-hand. If wire 6 must NOT be cut at all, send the five-finger hand alone. Speed matters — the display is at 3 and falling.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 6

Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👎 👍]

Parsing this round: Mute's eighteen signs slot perfectly into my seven questions. Q1 👍 — yes, my reading of the eleven-sign answer **was wrong**; Q2 👎 — the instruction is no longer "cut wire 6"; Q3 the corrected instruction in exactly my format: ☝×5 = wire 5, 🤏 = cut, 🖐 = end — **cut wire 5, the purple one, single cut**; Q4 👍 — Blind did report by voice; Q5 restates the identical instruction after that report — wire 5, cut, end — two independent slots agreeing; Q6 👎 — no timing condition, no reason to wait. Blind's signs confirm: six wires under the fingers, nothing changed, full report already given to Mute. And the board screams urgency: the display has gone 7, 6, 7, 4, 3, **0** — if that is a countdown, it has just emptied, and we are alive only because the cut hasn't happened yet. The rule is stable, double-confirmed, requires no waiting, and Blind's hands agree with my count. Every round of delay is the real danger now. I'm revoking wire 6 in the same breath — Blind must not touch it — and ordering the cut this round with the exact permission phrase, plus a post-cut protocol and a final verification gate Blind can perform instantly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — new order, and it supersedes everything I have said before. Do NOT cut wire 6. Mute's recomputed rule, after your voice report, is different, and Mute confirmed it twice in a row: the target is wire FIVE, the fifth wire counting from the keypad plate — the purple one. Verify fast: count wires from the keypad-anchored end, and stop at five. If your count reaches five wires with a sixth beyond it, that fifth one is the target. Then hear my permission: cut wire five now. Cut it cleanly, fully through, one motion, immediately — the display has just fallen to zero and Mute says there is no reason to wait. The moment it is cut: let go of everything, touch nothing else. Then report — thumbs-up if nothing changed after the cut; if anything happened, sounds, heat, vibration, the wires moving, send the call-sign once plus point-signs for how many things changed, and describe it all to Mute by voice. If your count under your fingers does NOT match six wires total with the target fifth from the keypad, do not cut — send me the count in point-signs instead. But if the count matches, cut wire five now. This is the go.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I read your eighteen signs as: yes, my earlier reading was wrong; no, it is not wire 6; corrected instruction wire 5 purple, single cut, end; yes Blind reported by voice; the rule restated identically — wire 5, cut, end; no timing condition. The double confirmation is received and I have just ordered Blind to cut wire 5 this round. The display now reads 0 — it has fallen 7, 6, 7, 4, 3, 0 — so if your manual says anything at all about what that display means or what happens at zero, sign me urgently next round. One question for the aftermath: the instant wire 5 is cut, what in the manual marks success — a light, silence, the display — and is there ANY follow-up action afterwards, anything pressed, entered or cut? Answer with thumbs-up for 'nothing further, the single cut finishes it' or the follow-up instruction in number-pinch-end format. You carried this bomb's rule from the manual to the hands that could act. If Blind and I are alive to hear it, your next signs are the last thing we need.")
```
